<strong>Comprueba con un punto.</strong>: Check with a point. Substituting a known point into the equation you have just obtained takes ten seconds and catches almost any slip in the working.
<strong>Dibuja siempre, aunque sea mal.<: Always draw, even badly. A freehand sketch with the data written on it rules out half the sign errors and shows which formula is needed. In space, drawing the axes and the direction vector is enough.
<strong>El producto escalar contesta a c: The scalar product answers almost everything. Perpendicularity, angle and projection all come out of it. If a question asks about an angle or a distance, start there before looking for a specific formula.
<strong>Elige la ecuación que menos trab: Choose the equation that gives least work. To intersect with a plane, the parametric form of the line; to see whether a point belongs, the general form. Changing form costs two lines and saves half a page.
Cada tramo aporta un número fijo de preg: Each section contributes a fixed number of questions, drawn at random from its topics without repeating a topic while that is possible, and avoiding the most basic exercises. With 12 topics and 10 questions, a single exam does not touch them all: that is why the link at the end reproduces the same exam, and “another exam” draws a different one.
Casi ninguna distancia de este bloque ne: Hardly any distance in this block needs a formula of its own. With the scalar and vector products they can all be derived, and deriving one scores the same as remembering it.
Cómo sacarle partido: How to get the most out of it
Dejo la pregunta: sin la fórmula exacta: I leave the question: without the exact formula it cannot be done
Distancia de un punto a una recta y a un: Distance from a point to a line and to a plane; the angle between lines or between planes; the symmetric point and the projection; identifying a transformation and composing two of them.
Doce temas que empiezan midiendo un triá: Twelve topics that start by measuring a triangle and end by intersecting two planes in space. This topic teaches nothing new: it asks. A procedural exam with exercises from the whole block, with a clock and no hints, to know whether the translation between the drawing and the equation —which is what this block is about— now goes both ways.
El enlace de un examen corregido reprodu: The link to a marked exam reproduces the same questions with the same numbers. A teacher can do one, copy the link and pass it to the class: everyone will sit the same exam and will be able to compare results and procedures.
Elige los tramos que entran. Las pregunt: Choose the sections to include. The questions are drawn at random from the exercises of each topic in the block, avoiding the most basic ones and without repeating a topic while possible. There are no hints: the marking and the step-by-step solution come on submitting.
Eso da la distancia a un plano perpendic: That gives the distance to a plane perpendicular to the line, which is not the same thing: it passes through any point of the line and the distance almost always comes out different.
Examen de geometría del plano y del espa: Exam on geometry of the plane and of space
Las dos salidas son buenas y ninguna nec: Both ways work and neither needs a new formula: the projection with the scalar product, or the area of the parallelogram divided by the magnitude of the direction vector.
Operar con vectores y calcular su módulo: Operating with vectors and computing their magnitude; going from the vector equation of a line to its general form; the relative position of two lines; identifying a conic and finding its elements from the equation.
Producto escalar, vectorial y mixto; ecu: Scalar, vector and triple products; equations of a line and of a plane; deciding whether two lines are skew, intersecting or parallel; the line that comes out of intersecting two planes.
Proyecto el punto sobre la recta y mido,: I project the point onto the line and measure, or I use the vector product
Sobre la puerta de la Academia de Platón: Over the door of Plato's Academy it was written, so tradition says, that nobody ignorant of geometry should enter. It was not a test of calculation: what was asked for was the ability to prove, and Euclid's Elements were used as a textbook for more than two thousand years, longer than any other. The habit of demanding the construction and not only the number is still alive in the exercises of this block.
Te piden la distancia de un punto a una: You are asked for the distance from a point to a line in space and you remember the formula for the plane. What do you do?
Un examen de bloque es un simulacro hech: A block exam is a mock paper taken at home: with a clock, no notes and no hints. The questions come from the exercises of the 12 topics of the block, spread across sections, and every time you start one the numbers are different and so are the topics: doing it several times covers the whole block. On submission everything is marked, the step-by-step solution of each question opens, and the mark comes out section by section, with links to what is worth revising. The “tailored to what you have done” option puts first what you have not solved yet: it is the way to check that no topic is left untouched.
Uso la fórmula del plano con el vector d: I use the plane formula with the direction vector as the normal
Ángulos en triángulos y paralelas; aplic: Angles in triangles and parallel lines; applying Pythagoras and deciding when you may; ratios of similarity and the intercept theorem; perimeters, areas, and the surface or volume of a solid from its measurements.
